To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

role stressors are a limiting factor for health care workers' change readiness and their overall withdrawal process; and colleague support moderates the relationship between role conflict, role ambiguity and role overload with change readiness.
role ambiguity and conflict are negatively related to change readiness and that colleague support mitigates the relationship between role conflict and change readiness.
role ambiguity, role conflict and role conflict were all negatively associated with change readiness, which in turn was related to withdrawal behaviours.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the factors that influence change readiness as well as the withdrawal process.
the impact of role demands and the role of colleague support on change readiness and withdrawal behaviours.
the impact of role demands on the withdrawal process and how these demands are moderated by social support from co-workers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
role stressors are a significant threat to the change process but that colleague support can mitigate their impact on change.
role stressors, particularly role ambiguity, have a negative impact on change readiness.
role ambiguity and conflict are the two most common role stressors in the health care sector that are associated with change resistance, whereas role overload is not.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
role ambiguity is the most detrimental to change readiness and the most likely to be moderated by colleague support.
role stressors can have both positive (change readiness) and negative (turnover intentions) effects on change and withdrawal behaviours.
role ambiguity and conflict are detrimental to change readiness and in the long term can lead to turnover intentions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
organizations should be cognisant of the impact that role stressors have on employees’ change readiness and their withdrawal process.
organizations should focus on mitigating role stressors and enhancing the role of colleague support to enhance change readiness and minimize the withdrawal process.
change readiness is an important mediator in the relationship between the stressors and the withdrawal process.
